sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Forge of the Giants** is a location in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: An enormous black cauldron atop a pedestal of octagonal black stone columns and solid rock, the Forge of the Giants overlooks the easternmost summit of the Mountaintops of the Giants. It is connected to Flame Peak by a hefty iron chain, held taut as if tethering the Lands Between in place. Two broken chains hang loosely at its side; a fourth once attached to the Forge's missing section. The inextinguishable Giants' Flame smolders quietly within the bowl, and colossal skeletal remains lie in the crevasse below.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
An ancient artifact of the Rauh civilization, the Great Forge contained the ever-burning power of the nameless fell god. The Fire Giants later claimed the forge when they invaded the Mountaintop, driving the Ice Dragons from their icy, windswept home. Sparks from the Forge of the Giants showered the frozen mountaintops, fertilizing the land with Fire Blossoms.

Long ago, Queen Marika ordered Lord Godfrey and his warriors to wage a war against the Giants, whose flame of ruin threatened her burgeoning age of the Erdtree. Marika's forces defeated the giants and confined the Flame, but it could not be fully extinguished. Marika cursed the last Fire Giant to tend it for all eternity.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.markdown: Melina instructs the Tarnished awaken the flame of ruin and commit the first Cardinal Sin. After either she or the Tarnished burns the Erdtree, the Tarnished is transported to Crumbling Farum Azula, where the Rune of Death is hidden.

sections.heading: Location
sections.markdown: The Forge of the Giants is accessible via Flame Peak after defeating the Fire Giant. The player teleports to Crumbling Farum Azula following a one-time cutscene at this location.

sections.heading: Forge of the Giants
sections.markdown: The Forge of the Giants Site of Grace is found on the eastern lip of the forge. If Melina has not left the player, the option to burn the Erdtree will be present. The **"Listen to the flames"** option will be present if not. Both options will cause the Erdtree to burn and transport the player to Crumbling Farum Azula.

sections.markdown:
- Alexander, Warrior Jar believes the flame of ruin can repair the crack he sustained in his duel with Starscourge Radahn.
- The Forge shares architecture motifs with the Divine Towers and Ancient Ruins of Rauh.
- The decoupled chains suggest the Lands Between was once part of a larger island. Whatever missing landmasses they connected to may be sealed or have drifted away.
 - Statues from the Ancient Dynasty show a bearded man holding half of an engraved tablet, with the other half at his feet. The tablet texture was sourced from the , the earliest known world map.
 - Alternatively, the Forge may have once been a portable smithery, suspended by chains like a hanging cauldron.
- The titan skeletons here are smaller than those in Caelid.
- Forge of the Giants is visible from the First Step in Limgrave.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Furled Finger** is a player role in Elden Ring's multiplayer.

Also called Cooperators, a Furled Finger is an ally or allies deliberately summoned to face and defeat an area boss alongside the summoner: a Host of Fingers. A summon makes themselves available by leaving a golden sign on the ground, which appears in other worlds for someone to touch and activate to bring the Furled Finger to their world. When they do so, they soon emerge in a swirling golden light and exhibit a soft, golden hue.

Players can make themselves available to be summoned using the Tarnished's Furled Finger while online. If a Host wishes to, they can use the Finger Severer to remove a Furled Finger from the session and send them back to their world.

sections.heading: NPC Summons
sections.markdown: While players can be summoned as Furled Fingers, even offline many in-game NPCs can be summoned from their golden sign on the ground. Most times, they are just outside the boss's arena before the fog gate, allowing time for the ally to appear and for the summoner apply buffs or change their equipment. In the case of a field boss like the Draconic Tree Sentinel, the signs are a short but safe distance away. Some summon signs are inside a boss arena, as is the case with Starscourge Radahn or Bayle the Dread.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Focus** is an resistance stat in Elden Ring.

Focus governs the Tarnished's ability to resist the build-up of Sleep and Madness. It will not decrease the amount of damage taken once afflicted by Madness.

The Tarnished's base Focus is the sum total of two different parts, with each part determined by their Level and Mind attribute. The first part is calculated based on the Tarnished's level. Their Focus will increase as they level up, with soft caps at level 71, 111 and 161. The second part is calculated based off of the Tarnishe's Mind stat, which will begin directly increasing the Tarnished's Focus from 31 Endurance and up. The total of these two parts is what is displayed on the status screen.

Raising Mind to increase Robustness has soft caps at 40 and 60 Mind.
- From 31-40 Mind: +3 Focus each level
- From 41-60 Mind: +0.5 Focus each level
- From 61-99 Mind: +0.25 Focus each level

Focus is further increased by equipping armor, which will display in the righthand column of the Status screen.

Focus can be temporarily increased by consuming Dappled Cured Meat.

sections.heading: Items that increase Focus
sections.markdown:
Directly
- Rift Shield, a small shield that increases Focus while equipped.
- Shield of the Guilty, a small shield that increases Focus while equipped.
- Spiralhorn Shield, a small shield that increases Immunity, Robustness and Focus while equipped.
- Eclipse Crest Greatshield, a greatshield that increases Immunity, Robustness and Focus while equipped.

sections.markdown: Ghost Gloveworts** are a type of bolstering material in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree. They are used to upgrade the power of Renowned Spirit Ashes.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: Ghost Gloveworts are a special incorporeal form of the white glovewort found growing in the many catacombs of the Lands Between. After Roderika becomes a spirit tuner at the Roundtable Hold, she can use Ghost Glovewort to incrementally upgrade the power and durability of Renowned Ashes up to a maximum of **+10**.

sections.heading: List of Ghost Glovewort
sections.markdown: There are **10** varieties of Ghost Glovewort to be found in the game.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Ghost Glovewort may be purchased from the Twin Maiden Husks at the Roundtable Hold after turning in Ghost-Glovewort Picker's Bell Bearings:
 - [[item:ghost-glovewort-picker-s-bell-bearing-1|Ghost-Glovewort Picker's Bell Bearing [1]]] unlocks the sale of Ghost Gloveworts 1, 2, and 3.
 - [[item:ghost-glovewort-picker-s-bell-bearing-2|Ghost-Glovewort Picker's Bell Bearing [2]]] unlocks the sale of Ghost Gloveworts 4, 5, and 6.
 - [[item:ghost-glovewort-picker-s-bell-bearing-3|Ghost-Glovewort Picker's Bell Bearing [3]]] unlocks the sale of Ghost Gloveworts 7, 8, and 9.
- Great Ghost Gloveworts are used to upgrade Renowned Ashes to +10, but only a limited number (**7**) can be obtained per playthrough.

sections.markdown:

- Revered Spirit Ashes improve the strength of spirit ashes summoned in the Realm of Shadow.
- Smithing Stones are used to upgrade standard weapons.

sections.heading: Additional features

- Added separate damage scaling for PvP.

Balance adjustments made within this feature will not impact single-player and cooperative play.

sections.heading: PvP Exclusive balance adjustments
sections.markdown:
The adjustments in this section do not affect single-player or cooperative play.**

- Increased stamina attack power in PvP for all attacks against guarded foes, except for long-ranged weapons.
- Improved poise damage in PvP for every weapon’s normal attack, except for Skills and long-ranged weapons.
- With a few exceptions, the power of Ashes of War in PvP has been lowered across the board.
- The power of the following incantations in PvP has been decreased:
 - Dragonfire / Agheel's Flame / Glintstone Breath / Smarag's Glintstone Breath / Rotten Breath / Ekzykes's Decay / Dragonice / Borealis's Mist / Unendurable Frenzy

- The speed and hit detection of Colossal Sword crouching and rolling attacks have been decreased.
- Increased the speed of some Colossal Weapon attacks.
- Decreased recovery time for Colossal Swords and Colossal Weapons, except for jump attacks, dual wielded attacks, and attacks while riding.

 - Celebrant's Sickle / Nox Flowing Sword / Shotel / Eclipse Shotel / Vulgar Militia Shotel / Scythe / Grave Scythe / Halo Scythe / Winged Scythe

- The poise rating of some attacks has been increased for the following weapons:

- The effects of the Greatshield Talisman and Hammer Talisman have been increased.
- Some effects of the spell Scholar's Shield, the Barricade Shield skill and the Shield Grease item have been adjusted as follows.
 - The effects on shields with low guard boost have been adjusted upward.

sections.heading: Notice of Update Distribution
sections.markdown:
The Colosseum awaits.

In this new update, a brand-new multiplayer feature in the form of the Colosseum arenas have been added, as well as new hairstyles for you to enjoy. Additionally, new balance adjustments have been made to improve the stability of gameplay.

sections.heading: **Major new features**

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Version 1.00** was a Game Version of Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Released on February 25, 2022, alongside the game itself, Version 1.00 was the initial retail build of *Elden Ring* and was only distributed on physical media. It is accessible exclusively by installing and playing the disc version of the game without an internet connection.

This version is notable for its many differences compared to later updates. It contains alternate icons, textures, dialogue, item descriptions, unused items, and different enemy placements. Several unseen characters were removed entirely, while others—such as the Gloam-Eyed Queen—were expanded upon in subsequent updates.

While much of the removed content supplements the final story without contradiction, some elements diverge significantly and may no longer be considered canonical.

sections.heading: Enemies

- Oracle Envoys had a different name and used blue Claymen Sorceries.
- Maliketh used unique purple particles for Destined Death attacks.
- Blackflame Monks used unique particles that resemble a mixture of Giants' Flame and Destined Death for their fire attacks.
- Deathbirds had a golden glow.

sections.markdown:
- Leyndell, Royal Capital lacked Oracle Envoys and Leyndell Knights, and was populated by Imps and Banished Knights, respectively. There were more Valiant Gargoyles.
- Deeproot Depths had bright golden lighting.

sections.markdown: Flames** are a common theme in the world of Elden Ring. Not limited to standard fire attacks, they come in a variety of colors with unique properties.

sections.markdown:

Deals Fire damage and gradually drains HP for a short duration.

Dark-red flame of the Formless Mother. Used by Mohg, Lord of Blood, his knights and reluctantly by Morgott, the Omen King.
Deals Fire damage and applies a build-up of Blood Loss.

sections.heading: Destined Death
sections.markdown:
Black and red-colored flame used by Maliketh and the Black Knife Assassins.
Deals Holy damage, reduces maximum HP and gradually drains HP for a short duration.

sections.markdown:
Violet flames of St. Trina, found only on St. Trina's Torch.
Deals Fire damage and applies a build-up of Sleep.

Deals Fire and Lightning damage.

sections.markdown:

Deals Fire damage and applies a build-up of Madness.

sections.markdown:

Deals Magic damage and applies a build-up of Frostbite.

sections.heading: Giants' Flame
sections.markdown:
Giants' Flame, also known as the Flame of Ruin or simply the Flame, is a red-orange-colored flame associated with the ancient Fell God of Fire. Used by the Fire Giants, derived by the Fire Monks, and seen by Erdtree Prophets through visions.
Deals Fire damage.

sections.heading: Glintstone Breath

The glintstone-infused flames spewed by the Glintstone Dragons.
Deals Magic damage.

Molten lava used by Magma Wyrms, Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, and Bayle the Dread.

It is wielded by Mausoleum Knights and their leader, Lhutel the Headless, and channeled by the legendary Eclipse Shotel of Castle Sol.

A flame with similar properties burns within Fia's Mist, a Death Sorcery conceived by Fia, Deathbed Companion. Prince of Death-Serving Omen and Commoners cast the spell at the Minor Erdtree in the Capital Outskirts, positioned above the Prince of Death's Throne in the Deeproot Depths.

sections.markdown: The **Fire Monks**, also known as the **guardians of the Flame**, are a faction in Elden Ring. They include the Fire Monks, Fire Prelates, the Guilty, and the Fire Giant.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The Fire Monks emerged during the War Against the Giants when they sided with young Marika against the Fire Giants. They used the Giants' Flame to protect her champions, allowing them to purge the Giants from Flame Peak. Afterwards, they were appointed guardians of the inextinguishable flame of ruin. They were sworn to protect the Golden Order and its Erdtree from the sealed Flame that once belonged to the Fire Giants.

The Monks were tasked with halting the surges and safeguarding the Giants' Flame secrets. Their work guaranteed that the Flame would never pose a threat to the Erdtree again.

Sorceries draw from the power imbued in glintstone. It is said that glintstone is the amber of the cosmos, and that it contains the vitality of the stars. Glintstones have a wide variety of applications: they can be embedded in staves used to cast sorceries, and the stone crowns worn by scholars of the Academy of Raya Lucaria Conspectuses; used as ornamentation in various weapons; or used as a receptacle for a sorcerer's soul after removal with a Primal Glintstone Blade. In addition, many glintstone sorceries conjure projectiles made of glintstone, which can be launched at enemies.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Frenzied Flame** (狂い火, *Kurui Hi*), also called **Yellow Flame of Frenzy** (黄色い狂い火, *Kiiroi Kurui Hi*) and **Yellow Flame of Chaos** (混沌の黄色い火, *Konton no Kiiroi Hi*), is a force that manifests in the eyes of those stricken by maddening grief and suffering. It is feared by many for its uncanny ability to destroy individuality, capable of melting away even eternal spirits. Those deeply stricken by its folly develop an insatiable need to spread its influence further, willingly seeking to infect others with it. These afflicted, known by some as Chaos Followers, yearn for the arrival of their lord so that they may incinerate all that divides and distinguishes.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
One of the unique properties of the flame, destroying individuality, manifests mainly in its ability to seemingly brainwash those it has afflicted. Many afflicted repeat the same cries and phrases despite never having interacted with one another (the most notable of these phrases being *"Melt it all away..."* and *"May chaos take the world!"* repeated ad nauseam). Seemingly blending their minds into a single, hivemind-like state.

A chosen few of those afflicted are capable of transforming into the Lord of Frenzied Flame after an apparent death, or some sort of transformation or rebirth process, it's not clearly stated and left to speculation. The strength of a lord can seemingly vary depending on who its original host was, with several individuals having proven capable of becoming one. However many of the afflicted were either too non-committal or physically feeble to accomplish anything, causing them to be considered frauds and failures in the eyes of their followers. Once a Lord of Frenzied Flame manifests, the head of the original host is replaced by a black hole with yellow flames spewing out of its core, completely erasing any trace of the original host's identity. However, if the Tarnished manages to inherit the flame, it's unclear whether his identity is truly erased. Given his ability to subdue demigods and gods like the Elden Beast, it is plausible that he did not succumb to the Flame, but instead mastered it—fusing with it rather than being consumed.

The origins of the flame are unclear, as the flame itself is said to have made its first appearance in the empty eye sockets of Shabriri, after his eyes were gouged out in punishment for slander. However, its incantations, the most powerful means that the flame manifests itself through, are also said to have come from the Three Fingers. It is also the clasp of Three Fingers that appoints a specific subject to become a Lord of Frenzied Flame.

Even without direct influence of the Three Fingers, the flame is capable of appearing on its own in sites of great suffering, such as the ninth campsite of Mt. Gelmir, where it has appeared in the eyes of Leyndell Soldiers suffering from the trauma of a particularly appalling battle. It has also appeared in the eyes of the surface-dwelling Nomadic Merchants, and while they are unable to settle and are forced to move around the lands constantly, their relative freedom gives them enough comfort to endure only minor symptoms, allowing some of them to have fairly normal conversations with passersby. They utter the mantras of the Chaos Followers only when attacked or dying.

Some have willingly pursued the Frenzied Flame in an attempt to use it as a powerful weapon, however every attempt to control the flame has ended in failure and left those who pursued it irreparably psychologically damaged. That said, even if the Tarnished chooses to purge himself from the Flame, he can still use the frenzy incantations in the pure form of a weapon, yet still susceptible to madness, however.

In a cruel twist of fate, the fear the world has for the flame has only supported its growth, as any attempt to quell it through the punishment and subjugation of its subjects has only intensified and worsened their symptoms, allowing the flame to fester more deeply into its hosts, becoming more powerful and widespread as their suffering increases. Primary example of this being the Golden Order's punishment of the Great Caravan, after they were accused of heretical beliefs, and the Hornsent's damnation of Midra and his entourage, after their attempt of studying of the flame. Both events would eventually lead to the near-or-complete successful manifestation of the Lord of Frenzied Flame.

sections.markdown: - The flame's ability to blend minds together may have been more apparent in an earlier version of Elden Ring. As the brotherhood of Nomadic Merchants that can be encountered throughout the world would mention that they fear going to sleep, as while asleep, they would feel as if their minds would rapidly drift and switch between each other, leaving all of them bewildered and confused on who they really are when they wake up.

sections.markdown: are Enemies in Elden Ring, included in the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC. They act like unmarked bosses, and do not respawn.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown:
Furnace Golems are animate metal cages of titanic proportions that contain a raging inferno of Messmer's Flame and the scattered sap from the Scadutree. Their thorny, iron bodies contain countless charred corpses locked in desperate, agonizing poses. They use their massive arms to catch enemies and dump them into their torsos. They reignite their kindling and burn brightly to incinerate their victims, which include animals and even dragons. Their kneecaps are adorned with Fire Giant hair and faces, and their "face" is a burning sun of horns in the image of the Fell God of fire, took from the hornsent's legends. Their faces are animated to show different expressions in reaction to taking damage.

Furnace Golems deal Standard, Strike, and Fire damage. They are weakest to Standard, Strike, and Magic damage. They are immune to all status ailments. They are especially vulnerable to Critical Attacks to their faces and Hefty Furnace Pots thrown into their bowls. Armored Furnace Golems are found at Charo's Hidden Grave and on the eastern Scadu Altus, north of the Bonny Village. Their legs are covered in highly durable metal armor, which protects them from physical attacks.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: A furnace hex powers the deadly and destructive Furnace Golems. The Messmer the Impaler used them as powerful weapons of war in his genocidal Crusade, where they aided his army in purging the Realm of Shadow of anyone who are impure and didn't bear the light of Grace and destroyed everything in their paths. The majority of Furnace Golems throughout the Realm of Shadow are now inactive, and though some are still operational.

- The Furnace Visage is placed high above the Fire Giant faces, implying the Fell God towered over them.

sections.heading: Overview

The Gate of Divinity is a mysterious place that can be used to elevate Empyreans into godhood under the correct circumstances. It has existed since ancient times, and is an incredibly holy site and artifact to the Hornsent, and is found at the pinnacle of their civilization: atop the tower of Enir-Ilim, crowning the settlement of Belurat. It is even necessary to pass through a ceremonial cleansing room in order to reach the Gate.

Despite these ties to the divine, the Gate itself is a ghastly construct. It is composed of countless corpses roughly pressed and fused together into two massive, misshapen columns and the base they sit upon. Bodies and viscera are also messily scattered about the large plaza directly in front of the Gate. At one time in the ancient past, the corpses comprising the Gate looked much 'fresher', and the Gate appeared red and slick with fresh blood. In the present, however, the Gate appears grey, faded, and calcified, and much of the viscera in the plaza is partly buried beneath encroaching sand dunes.

Before the Age of the Erdtree, an Empyrean and Numen woman hailing from the Shaman Village named Marika travelled to the Gate and ascended to godhood, becoming the vessel of the Elden Ring. Little is known of her ascension, though it occurred during the era when the Gate was still slick and red with blood, and involved her holding a mysterious golden strand aloft in the golden light at the Gate's centre. Her ascension led to the creation of the Erdtree and the Scadutree and ushered in a new era, with Marika becoming sovereign of the Lands Between and Godfrey becoming her spouse and the first Elden Lord.

Much later, following the death of Mohg, Lord of Blood, his corpse was stolen and transported to the Land of Shadow, where Miquella would require it for an ancient ritual. At the Gate of Divinity, Miquella ascended to godhood and resurrected Radahn, using the body of Mogh as a vessel. Miquella then blessed Radahn and made him his consort. The Tarnished then defeats Radahn and Miquella, preventing the latter's "Age of Compassion".

sections.heading: Secret Rite
sections.markdown: The Secret Rite Scroll details the workings of the Gate of Divinity's ascension ritual. An Empyrean can reach godhood by passing through the gate. However, they cannot return until the Gate summons the soul of a champion worthy of becoming Elden Lord and binds it to the body of another Lord candidate. Although the exact events that occur at these moments of ascension are unclear, those who meet the criteria return from the Gate in golden light, empowered as a true god.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Ghostflame Breath** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Communion Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Dragon Communion:** Limgrave / Caelid / Jagged Peak
- Acquired from the altar at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion on the Jagged Peak for 3 Dragon Hearts.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown:
The caster floats up into the air and summons a dragon head, before breathing out a wave of deathly mist, dealing Magic damage equal to 168% of Incantation Scaling and inflicting 55 Frostbite build-up up to 3 times (i.e. 504% of Incantation Scaling and 165 Frostbite build-up cumulatively) if the entire wave hits.

Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 60 points of Stamina to cast, and another 60 points upon using the follow-up breath.
- Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion.
- Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used.
- This spell can be cast midair but cannot be cast while mounted, unlike Dragonice.
- Of the three Frostbite-causing Dragon Breaths (this spell, Dragonice, and Borealis's Mist), this is the most cost-effective for Magic damage, but causes considerably less Frostbite build-up.
 - Compared to Dragonice, this spell deals 25% more damage but also consumes 20% more FP and causes 50% less Frostbite build-up.
 - Compared to Borealis's Mist, this spell deals 5% more damage and consumes 15% less FP but causes 50% less Frostbite build-up.
- Casting this spell until it stops costs 144 FP: 2*36 FP from the two breaths and 12*6 FP from keeping the spell running.
 - Only 79 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains as it will continue casting regardless.
- Deals 20% less damage against other players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Despite not being a named dragon breath, it behaves like one. This means that the caster floats in midair and that it cannot be cast when riding Torrent.
- This is effectively the second strongest "named" dragon breath attack, dealing 11% less damage than Smarag's Glintstone Breath and only 0.6% less damage than Agheel's Flame (the latter is only if an enemy's Fire Damage Negation and Magic Damage Negation is equal), and deals 8% more damage than Rotten Breath.
 - However, the, admittedly low, Frostbite build-up of the spell can even the field against non-immune enemies as it deals a significant amount of percentage-based damage and lowers their Damage Negation against further attacks.
- Patch 1.07 the power of the following incantations in PvP has been decreased.
 - The multiplier for damage against other players was lowered from 100% to 80%.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Oversized social insects that fiercely defend their underground tunnels, where they feast upon gathered human remains. Red and hairy, Giant Ants grapple their prey with powerful jaws to pierce them with abdominal stingers. They can expel highly-acidic venom in viscous clumps, which solidifies into Formic Rock deposits. Their acid spray has surprising range and bypasses a shield's guard.

Giants Ants can cling to walls and even ceilings in their lairs, dropping down to swarm and ambush intruders. Others march up and down the boughs of Great Trees, foraging for resources to support their colonies.

sections.heading: Variants
sections.markdown:
Giant ants come in a variety of different forms:
- Giant Ant
- Giant Ant (Medium)
- Giant Ant (Saddle)
- Giant Hardhead Ant
- Giant Honeypot Ant
- Giant Winged Ant

sections.heading: Saddle
sections.markdown: Saddled Giant Ants** are the reluctant mounts of Nox Swordstress, held in a trance placed by the Nox, indicated by glowing purple eyes. However, lulling the Ants to Sleep dispels the enchantment, freeing them to turn on their former masters.

sections.heading: Winged
sections.markdown: Giant Winged Ants** move faster and hover out of reach of melee attacks. Although they utilize exclusive airborne attacks, they are otherwise identical to their worker counterparts, using their moveset when grounded.

sections.heading: Hardhead
sections.markdown:
Giant Hardhead Ants**, also known as **Shield-Headed Ants**, possess enlarged, heavily-armored heads that act as nigh-impenetrable shields, making them resistant to damage and tough to stagger. Their bites can inflict Poison status, and they can spit globules of formic acid. If given the opportunity, they ram and knock enemies prone with a headbutt.

Their only weakness is their unarmored legs and abdomens, though they protect their bodies well in favorable positions.

sections.heading: Honeypot
sections.markdown:
Giant Honeypot Ants**, also known as **Large Giant Ants** and **Bloated Ants**, are a voracious, highly-specialized caste rendered immobile by their enormously plump, honey-filled abdomens. Frail and utterly defenseless, they gorge themselves in heavily fortified chambers at Ainsel River and Deeproot Depths, protected by their colonies.

This variant boasts a different set of Resistances than other Giant Ants; it is not as vulnerable to Fire damage, but is often slain with a single strike to its ballooned abdomen, which functions as a weak spot.

Honeypot Ants drop valuable items, such as Rune Arcs and Numen's Runes, but will not respawn once defeated.

- Triple Bite (avoided by double backstepping or rolling)

sections.markdown:

- The huge head of one of the giant ants which inhabit the two underground rivers, was used without modification as a shield, excelling at repelling enemy attacks. it also grants a boost to Immunity when wielding the shield
- Using the acidic rock dropped by the ants, a forbidden art of Depraved Perfumers releases an Acid Spraymist from user's mouth, damaging armaments and temporarily lowering Attack Power.
- Romina, Saint of the Bud, conceals an Ant's stinger.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Giant Ants are largely based on real-world ; each variant represents a different caste:
 - Giant Honeypot Ants are repletes, which store honey and sugar in their bloated abdomens for the colony to use. "**Honey**" is the filename for the Giant Honeypot Ant's abdomen.
 - Hardhead Ants are ants, likely based on soldiers, as they use their large, flat heads to seal colony tunnels and entrances.
 - Winged Ants are , mature ants that sprout wings and fly off to find mates and start new colonies.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Game Version **1.11** was an update that never released publicly. It is the patch that was distributed to game journalists and internet content creators so that they could make reviews for Shadow of the Erdtree in time for its public launch.

sections.heading: Differences from later versions
sections.markdown: This update never got any officially released patch notes from neither FromSoftware or Bandai Namco. However many reviewers made note of the Final Boss being significantly more difficult compared to the publicly released version, due to it having higher damage across the board along with one of its attack strings having such long hit-stun on each hit that once one attack in the string connected with the player then the entire rest of the string was guaranteed to land as well.

sections.heading: Map Changes
sections.markdown: It is also notable for having a different map design compared to the publicly released version. sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Furious Blade of Ansbach** is an incantation spell in Shadow of the Erdtree. It is one of the Blood Oath Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Loot:** Enir-Ilim
- Complete Sir Ansbach's questline while siding with him against Needle Knight Leda and defeat Promised Consort Radahn and then this Incantation (as well as Ansbach's Set and the Obsidian Lamina) can be found on his body, just to the right after entering the boss arena again.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
User dashes forward slightly before slashing twice in wide arcs with a bloodflame dagger to deal Fire damage equal to 97% of Incantation Scaling twice, before a wave of fire follows the path of the last slash to deal another burst of Fire damage equal to 154% of Incantation Scaling.

For the charged version, there are now three dagger slashes that deal damage equal to 98% of Incantation Scaling and the final burst deals damage equal to 163% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 37 points of Stamina to cast, whether charged or uncharged.
- Inflicts Blood Loss build-up, 180 for the uncharged version and 250 for the charged version.
 - Since all of the Blood Loss comes from bloodflame effects the build-up doesn't scale with Arcane, even if the Dragon Communion Seal is used.
 - For context, most enemies have a default resistance to Blood Loss of roughly 400 to 500, meaning the uncharged spell will most likely cause the Status Effect in 2-3 casts and the charged version will usually cause it within 2 casts, provided they are cast somewhat quickly after the other.
- Damage is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon when charged.
 - Since the damage of the dagger slashes already are increase by 1% the total increase is 16% for them, while the final burst has its damage increase by 6% and thus gets a total increase of 22%.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.13 increased attack power, fixed a bug where the “Furious Blade of Ansbach” Incantation did not apply Hemorrhage status build up.
 - For the uncharged spell the dagger slashes had their damage increased from 90% of Incantation Scaling to 97% of the same, and the final burst had its damage increase from 145% of Incantation Scaling to 154% of the same. The charged spell's dagger slashes had their damage increased from 90% of Incantation Scaling to 98% of the same, and its final burst had its damage increase from 145% of Incantation Scaling to 163% of the same.
- Patch 1.14 cancelling this incantation into rolls will now take less time, increased poise damage, increased enemy knockback distance.
 - For the dagger hits the poise damage was increased from 4 (68 against other players) to 5 (85 against other players) and for the wave of fire the poise damage was increased from 2 (34 against other players) to 3 (51 against other players).

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Ghostflame Dragons** are optional bosses in Shadow of the Erdtree. They are weak to both Holy damage and anti-dragon effects.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Ghostflame Dragons are undead drakes with the innate ability to wield Ghostflame, a trait they share with the Deathbirds.

Their skeletal frames are cloaked in tattered funerary cloth, their wings sparsely feathered, and scraps of decaying flesh cling loosely to their bones. These dragons are the remains of fallen drakes that drifted into the Realm of Shadow. They possessed such vivacity that they could not fully die, becoming Those Who Live in Death.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.markdown:
There are three Ghostflame Dragons in the Realm of Shadow:

- **Gravesite Plain**
 - Location: Near the Greatbridge, North Site of Grace.
 - Details: Found asleep in the center of a swamp upon first encounter. During phase 2, it gains the ability to summon Skeletons to assist it in battle.

- **Scadu Altus**
 - Location: In a clearing near the Moorth Highway Site of Grace.
 - Details: This Ghostflame Dragon is engaged in a skirmish with a battalion of Messmer Soldiers, Messmer Foot Soldiers, and Black Knights.

- **Cerulean Coast**
 - Location: South of the Cerulean Coast Site of Grace.
 - Details: This dragon dramatically swoops down from the sky during its initial encounter. It summons several Skeletons each time it uses its *Ghostflame Bellow* attack.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.markdown: All Ghostflame Dragons drop a Dragon Heart and a Somber Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.markdown: Ghostflame Dragons utilize a modified version of the standard Dragon movepool. Compared to other Dragons, they prefer to fight within melee range. Their Ghostflame breath attacks deal magic damage and apply Frostbite buildup.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Ghostflame Dragons count as both Dragon and Undead enemies.
 - Ghostflame dragons are weak to both Holy damage and anti-dragon effects.
- Defeating a Ghostflame Dragon will unlock Ghostflame Breath when performing Dragon Communion.
- Multiplayer and Spirit Ashes are allowed in all Ghostflame Dragon encounters.

sections.heading: Notes

- Attack Power is boosted by 3% when the Messmer's Helm is worn.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Giant Dogs** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: Giant Dogs are massive, monstrous hounds with oversized hind legs and underdeveloped forelegs. They are aggressive, fast enough to outrun mounted players, and lunge to bite with reckless abandon. They are exceedingly dangerous creatures with huge appetites.

sections.heading: Razor-Toothed
sections.markdown: These Giant Dogs have spikey white fur and razor-sharp teeth. The variants with red eyes howl upon detecting the player. This unique move alerts the other dogs to attack, much like the Foot Soldiers and Wandering Nobles with trumpets.

sections.heading: Snow
sections.markdown: Giant Dogs inhabiting the Mountaintops of the Giants are covered in snow and unafraid of the Beast-Repellent Torch.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.markdown:
- Giant Dogs are found throughout Caelid.
 - A unique variant wearing a spiked collar keeps watch outside of Gowry's Shack. This guard dog has a unique move where it sprays a cloud of Scarlet Rot.
 - A pair monitors a herd of hostile Sheep near the Shack of the Rotting.
 - A pack of Giant Dogs attack the Redmanes near Redmane Castle
- A small group has gathered on the incline leading to the Hermit Merchant's Shack in Greyoll's Dragonbarrow.
- Giant Dogs are found on the Mountaintops of the Giants, past the First Church of Marika.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Giant Dogs are vulnerable to many types of damage including Standard, Strike, and Fire.
 - They are highly susceptible to Sleep. A single Sleep Pot at Faith 22, Int 15 is enough to proc the status ailment.
- Giants Dogs have very low Poise and are easily Stance-broken, enabling a Critical Attack to the face.
 - Their stance can be broken with a single guard counter.
- Their attacks are easy to block or sidestep, despite their size and damage.
- Their attacks deal damage to other enemies, including other Giant Dogs.
- The standard variants are held at bay by the Beast-Repellent Torch; however, the red-eyed variants in Caelid and all snow variants on the Mountaintops of the Giants attack the player, regardless of the torch.

sections.markdown:
The **Giants' Flame** (巨人の火, *Kyojin no Hi*), also referred to as the **Flame of Ruin** (滅びの火, *Horobi no Hi*) and the **Flame of the Fell God** (悪神の火, *Akujin no Hi*), is a divine element in Elden Ring.

The flame of ruin is an ancient and inextinguishable fire capable of burning even the Erdtree itself. This power of the fell god is wielded as Giants' Flame incantations by Fire Giants and Fire Monks.

sections.heading: Background
Age of the Erdtree
sections.markdown:
The fell god's Flame was a forbidden subject during Queen Marika's reign. Although its presence was a native part of the Golden Order, it was anathema to Erdtree Worship. The Fire Monks were appointed to guard the Flame, and the path to the Mountaintops became Forbidden Lands. However, the Erdtree was fated to catch flame, and prophets who foresaw the cardinal sin were branded heretics and banished. The Fire Monks eventually succumbed to the Flame's allure, and worshipped it out of reverence and fear. The secrets of the Giants' Flame were documented in a Giant's Prayerbook and kept hidden by the Prelates. The Flame's ability to consume the Erdtree was later suppressed when Maliketh sealed the Rune of Death.

After the Shattering, Adan stole the Flame of the Fell God from Chief Guardian Arghanthy, and Fire Monks crusaded as far as Liurnia to reclaim it.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.markdown: The flame of ruin continues to smolder within the forge on the northern mountaintops. It can be rekindled to burn the Erdtree and its impenetrable thorns. This unlocks the road to Crumbling Farum Azula and Destined Death.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Some Fire Monks were captivated by the Black Flame, becoming Blackflame Monks.
- Only Melina or a Lord of Frenzied Flame may awaken the Giants' Flame.
- The fell god is said to inhabit the Giants' Flame.
- The champions of the Erdtree used Flame, Protect Me to bolster themselves during the War Against the Giants.
- A Flame within strengthens the body and cleanses poison and scarlet rot.
- Flame grants life to Burning Corpses.
- Giants' Flame is emulated by the Flame Chariots.
- The Furnace Golems use a variant of Flame.
- Messmerfire is closely related to the Giants' Flame.
 - Both resurrect Putrid Corpses
 - Messmer's Orb is nearly identical to the Flame of the Fell God.
 - Messmer's Kindling burns the Sealing Tree that shrouds Enir-Ilim.
 - Flare, O Serpent! follows the naming schema.
- Black Flame is closely related to the Giants' Flame.
- In the Chinese and Korean 1.0 version of the Sword and Night of Flame, Radagon is symbolized by Giants' Flame."

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Giants' Flame incantations**, also known as **Flame incantations**, are a type of Incantation spell in Elden Ring. These Fire-based incantations draw their power from the flame of ruin wielded by the Fire Giants of Flame Peak. They focus primarily on devastating attacks that can incinerate foes, unleash torrents of fire, or invoke protective flames to bolster the defenses and might of the caster. Many of these incantations demonstrate the raw, chaotic nature of fire, allowing for both area-of-effect damage and targeted assaults.

The Giant's Seal increases the effectiveness of offensive Giants' Flame incantations, except for Catch Flame, Fire's Deadly Sin, and Flame Sling.

sections.heading: Boosting Giants' Flame Incantations
sections.markdown:
Fire Scorpion Charm increases Fire Attack Power by 12% (8% in PvP).
- Flame, Grant Me Strength increases Fire Attack Power by 20% (15% in PvP) for 30 seconds as a Body Buff.
- Flame-Shrouding Cracked Tear increases Fire Attack Power by 20% (15% in PvP) for 3 minutes. 
- Giant's Seal increases Attack Power by 20% when held in an active hand, and by 44% when wielded in each hand. 
 - The Giant's Seal bonus does not apply to Catch Flame, Fire's Deadly Sin, or Flame Sling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown: - Catch Flame, Fire's Deadly Sin, and Flame Sling do not produce a spell sigil when cast, indicating they are not true Giants' Flame incantations. Instead, these spells are associated with prophecies involving the Cardinal Sin.

sections.markdown: Gladius, Beast of Night**, also known as **Tricephalos**, is a Night Lord boss in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Gladius is a massive, demonic wolf with three heads and an extra set of forelimbs. It swings around a greatsword on a long chain and launches massive fireballs. It can split its body into three one-headed, quadrupedal versions of itself, but only the original shadow retains the flail sword. The form change is signaled by a howling roar.

Gladius may be challenged by selecting "**Tricephalos**" as the expedition target at the Shrouded Roundtable Hold. It is confronted on the third day after traveling beyond the tree door at the Spirit Shelter. Tricephalos is the first Night Lord expedition and is unlocked by default. It deals Fire damage and is vulnerable to Holy damage.

sections.heading: Resistances
sections.markdown:
- Damage Types
 - +0% indicates that a boss is neutral to that damage type.
 - A positive value () indicates bonus damage.
 - A negative value ( ) indicates that a boss is resistant to the damage type.

- Resistances
 - A lower value indicates faster procs of the applicable status effect.
 - The **** symbol denotes full immunity to the status effect.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- This Nightlord is fought on the final day of the Tricephalos Expedition.
- This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its stance is broken.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Internal name: **NocturnalCerberus**.
- Gladius was first revealed in the initial trailer and was the only Nightlord featured in the network test.
- Among the Nightlords, Gladius is:
 - The first to be fought.
 - The last Everdark Sovereign to debut.
- The name *Gladius* derives from the Latin word for "sword," referring to the short, double-edged blades used by Roman soldiers from the 3rd century BC to the 3rd century AD.
- Its design draws heavily from , the three-headed hound of that guards the gates of the to prevent the dead from leaving. This makes Gladius a fitting choice as the first Nightlord to be fought.
- In Maliketh, the Black Blade's boss area at Crumbling Farum Azula, there is a statue of a young girl surrounded by three wolves below a prehistoric depiction of the Elden Ring.
- Gladius' story is similar to that of the spirits of the Lone Wolf Ashes summon. This item, alongside the Spirit Calling Bell, were delivered to the Tarnished by Ranni the Witch, who was entrusted to do so by Torrent's former master.
- Curiously, the Tricephalos' expedition's description compares Gladius to shadows, a term similar to the Shadowbound Beasts.
- One of Everdark Gladius' attacks is the exact same used by Heolstor the Nightlord, hinting that the latter was the swordsman in Gladius' backstory.
- Gladius is reminiscent of Sif from the *Dark Souls* series:
 - Both are massive wolves who wield great swords for their boss fights.
 - They each have a bond with a swordsman, whose sword they utilize.
 - Their names may have ties with the word "sword", with Gladius' being of Latin origin and Sif's arguably sounding similar to saif of Arabic origin.
- Gladius might also hold ties to the Red Wolves. Interestingly, Gladius is weakest to Holy, which instead deals the least damage to the red wolves.

sections.markdown: The **Foot of the Jagged Peak** is a subregion of the Realm of Shadow in Shadow of the Erdtree. This area of the map is revealed by Map: Southern Shore.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Foot of the Jagged Peak lies on the Southern Shore, connecting the Gravesite Plain to the Jagged Peak. This craggy region is characterized by brown grass, sparse trees with few branches, and a vibrant orange sky. Fierce winds whistle around massive stones that thrust upward from the rugged earth at sharp angles. This land has felt the Ancient Dragons' red lightning, and the lifeless remains of numerous lesser dragons litter the landscape.

To reach the Foot of the Jagged Peak, start from the Castle Front Site of Grace in front of Castle Ensis and head south to the Dragon's Pit. After defeating the Ancient Dragon-Man, exit via Dragon's Pit Terminus and travel southeast. The path diverges at a clearing where a Jagged Peak Drake lies sleeping:

- The wooded trail heading south is patrolled by Lightning Rams and Azula Beastmen. This route leads to the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion, where the colossal dragon's body rests. Beyond the dragon, Charo's Hidden Grave and the Cerulean Coast lie to the west.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **First Defense of Leyndell** was an event that occurred during the The Shattering in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: At some point while the alliance of the Shardbearers still ruled over Leyndell, Royal Capital, Godefroy the Grafted, an influential member of the Golden Lineage plotted to seize control of the capital. The demigod apparently managed to recruit an army that assumed strong enough for the attack. Godefroy also made use of the special characteristic of his Shaman flesh, grafting into his body parts of corpses in an attempt to gain more strength.

sections.heading: Battle
sections.markdown: Godefroy and his soldiers apparently moved in the direction of Leyndell but ended up fighting around the Second Church of Marika, in the middle of Altus and well distant from even the outer walls of the capital.. The demigod and his soldiers would suffer a complete defeat at the hands of soldiers of Leyndell with their leader captured by Knight Kristoff, a member of the Ancient Dragon Cult of the capital.

sections.heading: Aftermath
sections.markdown:
Godefroy was imprisoned in the Golden Lineage Evergaol with only his axe in a secluded area close to the Grand Lift of Dectus and guarded by Vulgar Militia men.
Knight Kristoff became an hero for his deed and earned the honor of Erdtree Burial. He chose to be laid to rest in the Sainted Hero's Grave, the catacomb for the warriors that took part in the War of the Ancient Dragons of whom he was a devout worshipper.

Though the capital was successfully defended, the event precipitated the deterioration of the sovereign alliance between the Shardbearers caused by the traces of the Night of Black Knives still lingering.
This would eventually lead to the demigods clashing against each other and the following wars of the Shattering.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Godefroy possessed the Godfrey Icon, a legendary talisman depicting Godfrey and Serosh, the patriarch and guide the Golden Lineage even during his imprisonment.
- It is possible that the soldiers and knights involved in the battle were buried in the richly decorated graveyard behind the Second Church of Marika and in a separate side graveyard close to it, as both these cemeteries and the sword monument in memory of the battle share the same pink flowers.
- The faction of the attackers is not explicitly confirmed, but Godefroy's involvement suggests that soldiers affiliated with the Golden Lineage and aligned with the rebel demigod were the main force.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Great Runes are mighty shards of the Elden Ring which were inherited by some of the demigods. The great strength they granted tainted the demigods, compelling them to war over control of the Lands Between.

The known Great Runes are as follows:

- *Ranni's Great Rune* (mentioned only)

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The Great Runes are the shards of the Elden Ring, currently making up the Golden Order, and represent the concepts of order and discipline that the demigods enforced on the physical world. They were inherited by some of the demigod offspring of Queen Marika the Eternal following the shattering of the Elden Ring. The mad taint of the newfound strength granted by the Great Runes precipitated the Shattering, wherein the demigods fought for control of the Lands Between. The demigods who inherited Great Runes were known as Shardbearers.

The Tarnished, upon returning to the Lands Between, were compelled by the Two Fingers to seek out demigods to relieve them of their Great Runes in order to become Elden Lord. The Tarnished required one Great Rune to be granted audience with the Two Fingers in the inner chamber of the Roundtable Hold. They also required enough Great Runes to repair the Elden Ring before the Two Fingers would permit them to enter Leyndell, Royal Capital to have an audience with Queen Marika to become Elden Lord. During the course of the game, this is two Great Runes, however since the Shardbearer Morgott, the Omen King guards the entrance to the Erdtree and must be killed to access it, they will have at least three when granted audience. Finger Reader Enia has only ever seen two Great Runes together once before this.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- When initially obtained by the player, a Great Rune (except the Great Rune of the Unborn) would be devoid of any benediction, and had to be taken to the Divine Tower mentioned in its description, whereupon it would be restored by interacting with the image of the Great Rune above the inert Two Fingers at the summit of the tower. Further, a Rune Arc was required for The Tarnished (Protagonist) to be granted the blessing of a Great Rune after restoring it.

- The Great Runes acquired by The Tarnished were used to repair the Elden Ring in at least one ending.

- It is unknown if the Rune of Death is considered a Great Rune or an Elden Rune.

- The Great Runes reflect the demigods that inherited them. For example, Morgott's Great Rune was proof that he was born of the Golden Lineage, and the rightful Lord of Leyndell. Mohg, Lord of Blood's Great Rune was soaked with accursed blood from his devout love for the wretched mire he was born into. Morgott's and Mohg's Great Runes were naturally similar due to their bearers being twins. Malenia, Blade of Miquella's Great Rune was half-rotted but infused with Malenia's spirit of resistance.

- Miquella of the Haligtree and Ranni the Witch are the only Shardbearers known to have discarded their Great Runes. The whereabouts of Ranni's Great Rune remain unknown. Miquella relinquishes and breaks his Great Rune after the Tarnished crosses into one of three areas of the Land of Shadow: the eastern half of Scadu Altus, the Rauh Base region, or Shadow Keep.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- "Great Rune" (GR) was the developmental codename for *Elden Ring*.
 - *Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice* contained Project "GR" assets.
- Proper names for various Great Runes were cut before release.
 - Rune of Life - In the Chinese and Korean 1.0 text Helphen's Steeple, the Golden Order Greatsword, and Icon Shield make reference to the Rune of Life, which provides the Erdtree's power and places a curse upon heroes of the Lands Between. It is presumably Marika's own Great Rune.
 - Rune of Abundance — The cut Abundance Twinblade and Abundance and Decay Twinblade, weapons make reference to "the Rune of Abundance" and the "the Rune of Decay" in their descriptions belonging to Miquella and Malenia respectively.

 - Rune of Mind — In the Korean 1.0 text, the Dark Moon Greatsword refers to "the Rune of Mind" ("정신의 룬, *jeongsin-ui lun*), presumably Ranni's Great Rune.
- In English, Enia calls the player a Shardbearer after they acquire a Great Rune, while in Japanese she calls them .

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Greater Will** is an unseen character in Elden Ring. It is a mysterious entity hailing from the lightless void and serving as the dominant force in *Elden Ring* and the history of the Lands Between. Its vassals and envoys are central to the Golden Order. Its image boosted Intelligence and Arcane.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Long ago, the Greater Will fractured the One Great, creating births and souls. The adherents of the Three Fingers consider this action to be a mistake, because it resulted in torment, despair, affliction, sins, and curses.

The Greater Will sent a star bearing its gleaming daughter to the Lands Between. It communicated with Metyr, Mother of Fingers, through the microcosm held between her tail fingers. Soon, a second, golden star containing an Elden Beast arrived in the Lands Between. This Elden Beast was the Greater Will's vision for Order, and it would later become the Elden Ring. This beast was its vassal, and the living incarnation of the concept of Order. The Greater Will has other vassals and envoys known as the Two Fingers, who speak in a cipher sign language of light.

sections.heading: Eternal Cities
sections.markdown: Before the age of the Erdtree, the denizens of the Eternal Cities rebelled against the Greater Will. To shield themselves from its influence, the Nox donned ritual mirrorhelms to block its intervention and that of its vassals. In an act of blasphemy, they drew the ire of the Greater Will by wielding the Fingerslayer Blade against one of its vassals. In response to this transgression, the Greater Will unleashed Astel, whose destruction of the Eternal Cities condemned them to an existence underground.

sections.heading: Age of the Erdtree
sections.markdown:
During the age of the Erdtree begun by Queen Marika the Eternal and at least the era immediately preceding it, the Greater Will's envoy Two Fingers selected Empyreans as candidates to become the God of the coming age. Queen Marika was one such candidate, and created the Golden Order by confining the Rune of Death. However, Marika would eventually shatter the Elden Ring, leading to her demigod offspring inheriting the Great Runes which in turn would trigger a war known as the Shattering. The Greater Will abandoned the demigods following the Shattering, as none managed to claim title of Elden Lord.

According to the Two Fingers, the Greater Will has not abandoned the realm, nor the life that inhabits it, proclaiming this is why the Tarnished have been extended the Guidance of Grace. After the Tarnished returned to the Lands Between following the Shattering, the Two Fingers, at the behest of the Greater Will, bade them kill the demigods in order to claim their Great Runes to become Elden Lord by becoming Marika's consort, as the Greater Will had long since renounced the demigods.

In the time of The Tarnished (Protagonist), it was discovered that the entrance to the Erdtree was blocked by impenetrable thorns, preventing anyone from becoming the Elden Lord. This caused the Two Fingers to commune with the Greater Will in search of answers, which may take thousands or tens of thousands of moons. When The Tarnished (Protagonist) suggested burning the Erdtree, which would unbind Destined Death and slay the world itself, Finger Reader Enia exclaimed that the Fingers and the Greater Will would never allow it.

After The Tarnished (Protagonist) caused the Volcano Manor's recusants to disband following the defeat of Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, the recusant known as Knight Bernahl declared himself the inheritor of his comrade recusant's will. He declared their refusal to become the Greater Will's pawns and swore it would fall by his blade.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The Greater Will is never directly referred to as an Outer God in the game. Instead the Two Fingers selected both Ranni and her Dark Moon and Malenia and her Rot as potential candidates for godhood and to forge a new Order through the Elden Ring
- The Nox Mirrorhelms presumably worked by reflecting the Greater Will and the Two Fingers' language of light.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Godwyn the Golden**, also known as the **Prince of Death,** and **First of the Dead**, is a character in Elden Ring. He was a Demigod who suffered a spiritual death on the Night of Black Knives. In the absence of a soul, his body transformed into the Prince of Death. His Erdtree Burial contaminated the Greattree roots with Deathroot, giving rise to Those Who Live in Death.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown: The golden-haired Prince of Death has grown to immense size, developing a scaly fish tail and webbed forearms reminiscent of basilisks. His face has warped into a grotesque, fungal-like disk, and his eyes are drained of color. Death Blight erupts from his body, drawing swarms of buzzing flies. He remains locked in the posture of his death, as if still propped up by his assassins. He wears bracelets and a tattered blue robe adorned with red and gold floral patterns.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Godwyn was born during the Age of the Erdtree to Queen Marika the Eternal and her first consort, Godfrey, making him a scion of the Golden Lineage. He emerged as a hero of the Erdtree after the end of Age of Plenty when the Ancient Dragon Gransax breached the walls of Leyndell, triggering the War of the Ancient Dragons. Godwyn played a pivotal role during the final battle with Fortissax outside Leyndell. He prevailed, but spared the dread dragon, forging a friendship that ended the war and founded the Ancient Dragon Cult.

The dragon cult worshiped the ancient dragons and studied their lightning incantations. These practices were sanctioned by the Golden Order, as lightning and Gravel Stones were imbued with gold. Godwyn learned to channel Fortissax's power to summon a storm of golden lightning. His inner circle of elite ancient dragon knights formed his personal guard, who received the largest amber medallions ever bestowed.

sections.heading: Death
sections.markdown: Godwyn was the first Demigod to die in recorded history, perishing on the Night of Black Knives. His stepsister, Lunar Princess Ranni, orchestrated the plot by stealing a fragment of the Rune of Death from Maliketh and produced godslaying daggers imbued with Destined Death. The Black Knife Assassins infiltrated the royal capital and struck Godwyn, carving the half-wheel centipede into his flesh while a matching mark was etched into Ranni. The ritual caused both to suffer an incomplete death: Ranni's soul endured while her flesh destroyed; Godwyn's body remained, but his soul was gone.

sections.heading: Prince of Death
sections.markdown:
The soulless body of Godwyn the Golden was buried below Leyndell at the base of the Erdtree's roots, located in the Deeproot Depths. However, his spirit could not return to the Erdtree because he did not experience a true death. Godwyn's soulless body then grew and transformed into an unrecognizable, piscine aberration known as the Prince of Death. Ancient Dragon Fortissax entered Godwyn's Deathbed Dream to fight against the Death within him, but was ultimately corrupted by the Death Blight.

Through Godwyn, the Rune of Death seeped into the Greattree roots and spread throughout the Lands Between. Soon after, the Death-Prince's distorted visage manifested itself across the realm. His eyes peered out of tendrils and vines, and even his distorted face materialized in places of Erdtree burial. This corruption sprouted Deathroot, giving rise to Those Who Live in Death. Later, the roots of the Erdtree were disconnected from those below.

Wandering Mausoleums prowled the lands to recall the spirits of the soulless Demigod. Many lordsworn warriors protected these great Spirit Calling Bells, and willingly beheaded themselves in a Death rite to guard them eternally as Mausoleum Knights. Though the earth shook when the Mausoleums tolled, the spirit of Godwyn never returned. In contrast, Godwyn's innermost circle embraced his death and became the Death Knights, who quested for a cadaver surrogate to bring about the Age of the Duskborn.

Godwyn's downfall catalyzed the shattering of the Elden Ring and the subsequent Shattering War of the Demigods. Later, the knights of Castle Sol and Miquella worked toward achieving an eclipse they believed would restore Godwyn's soul to his body. Despite their efforts, the failure of the plan contributed to the doom of the Haligtree.

sections.heading: Game Events
sections.markdown: Fia, Deathbed Companion was the guardian of Those Who Live in Death. After recovering the half-wheel centipede taken from Godwyn's body, she makes her way to the Prince of Death's Throne. If Fia acquires the cursemark from Ranni's body, she sleeps with Godwyn to transfer to him the strength of countless heroes and grant him a second life as the Prince of Death. If Lichdragon Fortissax is defeated within the Deathbed Dream, Fia is free to transfer the spiritual warmth and vigor of her champions to the Prince of Death. As a result of their union, she conceives the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince. She requests it be used to mend the shattered Elden Ring, integrating the principle of Life within Death into the Golden Order and ushering in an Age of the Duskborn.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.markdown:
- Godwyn's transfigured main body rests at the Prince of Death's Throne, located in a shallow pool of purple water at the base of a tainted root in the Deeproot Depths. It also appears within the Deathbed Dream version of the area.
- Lesser versions of Godwyn can be found at Fog Rift Catacombs, Scorpion River Catacombs, and beneath Stormveil Castle.
- Godwyn's eyes seem to appear on Death Crabs and clumps of deathroot in tainted areas across the Lands Between, such as Summonwater Village, Tombsward Catacombs, and Wyndham Ruins.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Although the Prince of Death is the source of the Death Blight, he and the Prince of Death's Throne game area are harmless to the player.
- Godwyn was protected by a personal entourage in addition to the royal palace guard.
- After Godwyn's death, his closest allies did not agree on how to continue serving him. Godwyn's inner circle of golden knights embraced the Prince of Death and became his Death Knights, while Fortissax fought to stop the Death within his body.
- Godwyn's larger manifestations found at Fog Rift Catacombs, Scorpion River Catacombs, and Stormveil Castle are presumably the cadaver surrogates sought and protected by Death Knights.
- The Prince of Death's Pustule and Prince of Death's Cyst depict the duplication of his facial features. His cystic visage grows on the backs of Death Crabs and Giant Death Crabs living in tainted waters.
- Corpses clump together to form certain Prince of Death objects. They are likely a participating in a form of regression, similar to the gravestone accretions.

sections.markdown:

- The Prince of Death's grotesque, semi-circular face is reminiscent of (also known as bracket or shelf fungi) that grow on dead and dying trees.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Frenzied Flame Proscription** is a Site of Grace located within the Lands Between in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Frenzied Flame Proscription lies at the bottom of a catacombs in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds, deep below Leyndell, Royal Capital. This area can only be accessed after defeating Mohg, the Omen at the Cathedral of the Forsaken. The path is concealed by an illusory wall at the altar, leading downward. However, the route is sealed off by Morgott, the Omen King, accessible only after his defeat at the Elden Throne.

The area is filled with countless mummified Nomads who play a haunting melody on their stringed instruments. The Great Caravan were immured here by Queen Marika after they were accused of harboring the Frenzied Flame. In their despair, they summoned the Three Fingers.

After navigating down the beams, jump to the bottom; the floor will collapse, delivering the Tarnished to the eponymous Site of Grace. An illusory wall opposite the Grace conceals a treasure chest containing a Rune Arc. A second illusory wall reveals a hidden path to the Deeproot Depths near the Root-Facing Cliffs Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Lord of Frenzied Flame
sections.markdown:
Warning**: Meeting the Three Fingers locks the player into the "Lord of Frenzied Flame" ending, an action that may only be reversed by using Miquella's Needle.

The smoldering stone door can be opened after the player unequips all Armor, initiating a cutscene in which the Three Fingers bestow the power of Frenzied Flame. Interacting with the Three Fingers causes Melina to leave permanently, vowing to kill the player Tarnished. However, the player can bypass her sacrifice by using the Fingers' flame as kindling to awaken the Flame of Ruin at the Forge of the Giants and commit the Cardinal Sin. The player can still meet the Three Fingers if they have already used Melina to burn the Erdtree. The Three Fingers do not clasp the player again if they cheat fate by inserting Miquella's Needle at the storm beyond time.

If her questline has been advanced, Finger Maiden Hyetta will wait patiently on the side of the hall opposite the Site of Grace. She urges the Tarnished to seek an audience with the Three Fingers, whose sanctum lies beyond a large stone door that was partially melted by searing fingerprints. The door may only be opened once and only after unequipping all armor. After receiving the Flame of Frenzy, speak with Hyetta, who can then interpret the words of the Fingers to their chosen Lord of Frenzied Flame.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Forges** are landmarks in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
There are three ruined forge dungeons in the Realm of Shadow, each accessible from the overworld. These locations do not have bosses. Instead, an important item is looted from a large forge located at the end of the area.

The forges are filled with finished weapons and smoldering anvils. They were constructed many ages ago, when smithing was considered an act of divine significance. These sweltering workshops are home to Molten Tears, and are still operated by tireless Golem Smiths, who imbue smithscript weapons with souls.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown: - The Gas Stones found in forges were once used as fuel.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown: - There is a fourth, nameless forge dungeon in the game files.
